thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: write errors spike in prod after rollout (release/2026-03-15/blue). Error shows constraint failures and stopped migrations on a subset of hosts. Paging oncall. thread_ts=2389901234
jun: I’m on it — paging SRE and DB eng. Where are the error samples?
sasha: seeing a lot of 500s with payload: \"pq: duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"user_email_key\"\" and also some \"null value in column \"account_id\" violates not-null constraint\" logs. Hit after we ramped to 30% traffic ~10:20 UTC.
lina: that aligns — the migration we shipped added not-null on account_id without a backfill in stable path. Canary at 2% had no writes and passed. Staged rollout exposed real write traffic.
jun: ok immediate mitigation options: (1) flip feature flag to stop new code path, (2) rollback release, (3) run online backfill + quick migration. Which is fastest?
oliver: feature flag flip is fastest. I can hit the admin API now. If flag off, existing code path should accept writes. But some services already wrote rows expecting the new column; we might still have inconsistent rows.
sasha: rollbacks are risky because the DB changes are in the release package. We didn't migrate schema forward-only? What exactly ran on the DB? Lina, did the migration add the NOT NULL constraint or add a column+constraint?
lina: migration created column account_id (nullable) then ALTER set NOT NULL in the same deploy job. The canary jobs ran the schema change on the small pool, and the check passed; but there are background workers that were still running and hit the new constraint. The ALTER is blocking on some shards and is currently 'stuck' in an idle state: `pg_stat_activity` shows a long-running ALTER waiting on locks.
jun: can we cancel the stuck ALTER safely?
lina: if I cancel it, it'll rollback and free locks. But any writes that relied on the column being present will fail if code expects it. However flipping the flag reverts writes to old code path. Recommended: flip feature flag now, cancel ALTER, then plan a safe backfill and re-run migration during a low-traffic window.
oliver: I’m about to flip in feature-flag service. Command (internal):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://flags.redwood.internal/flags/enable -d '{"flag":"new_account_column","enabled":false}'
```
I'll run it now.

oliver: done — flag flipped to OFF :white_check_mark:. Can the app team confirm new writes are hitting the old path?
sasha: sending smoke: posting test create-account on prod canary tenant... getting 200 on old path. Error rate drop from 7% -> 0.8% on write endpoints (last 2m).
incident-bot: Metric: write_errors.prod 7.1% -> 0.9% after flag flip.
jun: good. Lina, cancel the ALTER and check lock holders.
lina: cancel initiated. Found two stuck sessions from rollout job runner (pid 14231, 14259). Killed them. ALTER rolled back cleanly. No locks now. Running quick validation query to find rows with NULL account_id that would fail under NOT NULL: 
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE account_id IS NULL;
```
Current count: 3,412 rows (mostly recent writes in last 10m).
sasha: so those will be fine under old code path. We still need plan for backfill.
jun: customer impact? support?
support-bot: Incident routed to support. We have three enterprise customers on dedicated infra that reported "save failed" errors starting ~10:22 UTC. Estimated affected requests: ~4.5k -> 2.1k errors until flag flip. No full outages; transient write failures. Already notified customer success for customers A, C.
oliver: immediate next steps I propose: 1) keep flag OFF / halt rollout, 2) mark release as halted in release tracker, 3) schedule backfill + re-run schema migration during off-peak and follow online migration pattern (batch backfill, add constraint with VERIFY USING or use temporary default), 4) postmortem and release checklist update.
jun: agree. I'll make the release halted and coordinate ticket. Lina, can you prepare backfill job and estimate runtime?
lina: backfill script ready; will run in parallel workers. Estimated time for 3.4k rows is ~5 minutes, but I want to run a dry-run on staging. For safety, plan 30 minutes including verification and small rolling disruption to consumers. Steps I suggest:
1) run backfill: `UPDATE users SET account_id = <inferred_value> WHERE account_id IS NULL;` (we have logic to infer via legacy_user_meta).
2) re-run ALTER to set NOT NULL WITH LOCK TIMEOUT and verify.
3) monitor errors and SLOs.
jun: do we need to rollback app binary? Not if flag off. We'll keep old code path active.
sasha: I'll keep monitoring and if anything else pops up we will rollback. Also we should check for any tenants that already wrote invalid payloads that may cause duplicates when backfilled.
lina: good point — there are 24 rows flagged as potential duplicate email conflicts during backfill. I’ll coordinate dedupe policy: for duplicates we queue for manual review and rollback conflicting writes. That number is small, won't block constraint set.
oliver: I updated release page and added a blocker note: rollout paused. Asking PMs to delay next wave.
jun: I'm going to notify exec on-call and create incident ticket INC-2026-0315-db-rollback. Handoff: I'm staying on call for the next 40 minutes to supervise backfill; if anything critical occurs I'll escalate. After the backfill and verify we can re-enable the rollout gradually with preview flags.
sasha: monitoring: writing a Kibana query and dashboards for user.create errors + constraint logs. Also added an alert threshold at 1% errors to trigger this channel.
incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff scheduled in 35m. Use /handoff when ready.
support-bot: Customer comms draft: "We've mitigated an issue introduced during a partial rollout that caused write errors for a small subset of customers. We have paused the rollout and implemented a fix; we'll follow up after verification." Approving with ops.
jun: timeline: flag flipped 10:24 UTC, ALTER cancelled 10:26 UTC, backfill starts 10:33 UTC, estimate done 10:40 UTC, verify + set constraint 10:50 UTC. I will update last_message_ts when done.
lina: backfill started (job id bf-238990). Running with 8 workers. No errors so far.
sasha: error rate steady at 0.7% and trending down. No new customer reports.
jun: ok — prepping post-incident items: ticket, timeline, owners. Once we confirm constraint can be re-applied safely, we'll schedule a controlled rerun with a canary that includes write traffic.
oliver: will also add a release checklist item: "Run backfill before toggling NOT NULL" and require DB eng sign-off.
jun: handing off in 30m to @sasha for monitoring. If nothing else, we'll close incident after verification and a short watch window.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged and mitigation in progress. Handoff planned. thread closed pending verification.
